## AI Tooling Turbulence: Ollama Breaks SillyTavern

The most significant technical development this cycle involves the breaking change in Ollama’s API, which has sent ripples through the local LLM community. Users discovered that Ollama now rejects requests containing the "p" flag, a parameter that was previously standard but is no longer required by the updated service. This oversight caused immediate connectivity issues for SillyTavernAI (ST) users, as their interface continued sending the legacy flag.

The friction highlights the ongoing tension between rapid backend updates and frontend stability. While some users wait for the ST fork to patch the incompatibility, others have already migrated to running `llama.cpp` directly as a stable workaround. This incident serves as a reminder for users managing their own AI infrastructure to keep an eye on dependency updates.

## Vintage Arcades & Tech Nostalgia

On the retro-tech front, two distinct threads captured attention. First, @台羽正 shared detailed analyses of classic arcade marquee art, focusing on Taito’s *Metal Black* and Seibu Kaihatsu’s *Raiden*. The discussion appreciated the vivid marketing visuals: *Metal Black*’s dynamic sci-fi imagery featuring a monstrous alien against a purple and orange sky, and *Raiden*’s bold red-and-black design claiming to be a "next-generation shooting game" with two-player support. These posts serve as a visual archive of 1990s arcade marketing.

Simultaneously, 4chan’s /p/ board sparked a debate on the modern utility of traditional camcorders, specifically the Canon XAVC 4K. While some users argued that professional ENG (Electronic News Gathering) remains the only viable niche, others pointed out the camera's enduring value for documentaries and concerts due to its optical zoom and battery life. A sentimental undertone emerged, with users linking the 20x zoom to national memory and nostalgia. Contrasting this, "zoomer" filmmakers are noted abandoning dedicated camcords for full-frame hybrids, prioritizing shallow depth-of-field and cinematic aesthetics over the reliability of traditional optics.

## Touhou Project Fandom

The Touhou community remained active with fan art and memes. A recurring meme featuring Keine Kamishirasawa, captioned "Keine doesn't mind explaining again," circulated widely, highlighting the character’s role as a patient history teacher. Meanwhile, new artwork surfaced, including "Sanae's Unexpected Affection," which explored Sanae Kochiya’s emotional side. On the more labor-intensive end of fandom, user @TouhouMaleGuy shared a SinSack piece that took over 12 hours to complete across seven layers, joking that they would not be drawing other Touhou girls for the foreseeable future.

## Synth Culture & Pokémon Quirks

In niche cultural updates, the "SineWavesOnSunday" radio show announced a repeat broadcast of highlights from the Synth East Festival, featuring electronic improvisation by a former snooker player and sets from artists like Scanner and e.m. arson. Elsewhere, Tumblr users humorously analyzed Joltik, noting that despite its tick-like design and swarm ability, it lacks a direct bite attack, leading to playful warnings about its potential to transmit Lyme disease.

## Quick Hits

*   **Camera Specs Debate:** On 4chan’s /gear/ board, users argued that "gear only matters if your photo doesn't suck." The consensus discouraged pixel-peeping, noting that artifacts like moiré are rarely visible in practice and that contentment with existing gear, such as the "6700," is the true path to photographic joy.
*   **Lobsters Tech News:** The mrncciew.com community shared a technical post on Wi-Fi PCAP analysis for macOS, indicating continued interest in network diagnostics within the tech-focused "Lobsters" ecosystem.
*   **Lisp on Mastodon:** A single item tagged #lisp appeared on Mastodon, though details remained sparse.
*   **Unsorted Items:** Approximately 285 items failed to cluster into these topics, including various minor updates and cross-posted content.

representative_texts: @台羽正 (tadashidaiba.bsky.social) —  This is a vibrant, dynamic advertisement or promotional poster for the arcade video game "Metal Black," published by Taito. The image is tilted slightly clockwise. The artwork depicts an intense science fiction scene set against a dramatic sky filled with swirling clouds in shades of deep purple, magenta, and bright orange, suggesting either dawn or dusk. Central to the composition are two main subjects: 1.  On the left, a large, monstrous alien creature lunges forward. It has a reptilian or dinosaur-like head with a gaping mouth full of sharp teeth, a scaly, textured body in hues of blue and grey, and what appear to be mechanical or armored segments along its back and limbs. Its eyes are glowing red. 2.  On the right, a sleek, dark grey futuristic spaceship is angled diagonally, pointing upwards towards the top right corner. The ship has a streamlined, angular design with visible thrusters emitting bright blue-white light trails as it flies. In the background behind the ship, a futuristic city skyline with tall skyscrapers is faintly visible under the colorful sky. The title "METAL BLACK" dominates the lower portion of the image. "METAL" is rendered in bold, blocky, metallic-blue letters with a white outline. "BLACK" is written in a larger, stylized, graffiti-like font in a gradient of light to dark blue, also with a white outline. Below "METAL," the Japanese katakana "メタルブラック" (Metaru Burakku) is written in smaller white text. Overlaid on the upper center of the image, running vertically, is large white Japanese text with a black drop shadow: "最終平和兵器。" (Saishū Heiwa Heiki - Final Peace Weapon). Beneath it, in smaller white text, is the tagline: "戦闘準備完了。僕らは、もう、引き返せない。" (Sentō Junbi Kanryō. Bokura wa, mō, hikikaesenai. - Combat readiness complete. We can no longer turn back.) Red, paint-splatter shapes are scattered across the image, particularly around the top and left edges, adding to the energetic and aggressive feel. In the top right corner, the Taito logo is present, with the text "キャッチ・ザ・ハート" (Kyacchi Za Hāto - Catch the Heart) above it. A small "TM" trademark symbol is visible near the right edge of the "BLACK" title.

@台羽正 (tadashidaiba.bsky.social) —  This image is the arcade cabinet marquee (top display) for the 1990 video game *Raiden*, developed by Seibu Kaihatsu, Inc. **Visual Composition:** - The layout uses a striking color palette of bright red and black. The background is predominantly black with a large, vertical red rectangle in the center containing the main artwork and text. - **Top Section (Red Background):** - At the very top, copyright text reads: "©1990 SEIBU KAIHATSU, INC.," - Large white Japanese characters: “超・原・点” (Chō Gen Ten - Super Original Point). - Below this are smaller lines of Japanese text: - “シューティングは今、新時代を迎える。” (Shooting games are now welcoming a new era.) - “原点に戻り、原点を超えた、” (Returning to the origin, surpassing the origin,) - “次世代シューティングゲームついに登場!!” (The next-generation shooting game finally appears!!) - Two wireframe illustrations of fighter jets are shown in profile, facing left. One is above the central text block, and a more detailed one is below it. - A yellow, starburst-shaped graphic on the left contains Japanese text: “二人同時プレイ 途中参加可能” (Futari dōji purei, tochū sanka kanō - Two-player simultaneous play, mid-game join possible). - **Middle Section:** - The words “VIDEO GAME” appear in white above the title. - The game’s title, “RAIDEN,” is displayed in large, stylized, gradient blue-and-white lettering with sharp, angular edges. - Below the title is the Japanese Katakana for the game’s name: “ライデン” (Raider). - A small “TM” trademark symbol is visible to the right of the title. - **Bottom Section (Red Background):** - Three rectangular screenshots from the game are displayed side-by-side, showing gameplay of a top-down shooter with a jet firing at enemy formations. - **Very Bottom (Off-White Beige Strip):** - Company name: “SEIBU KAIHATSU, INC.,” and its Japanese equivalent “有限会社セーブ開発” (Yūgen-gaisha Seibu Kaihatsu). - Address: “〒101 東京都千代田区三崎町2-20-1” - Phone/Fax numbers: “TEL 03(238)9169 / FAX 03(238)9187” In summary, this is a promotional graphic for a classic arcade shooter, highlighting its visual style, two-player cooperative mode, and technological claims for its time.
clusters.summary: Two recent posts by @台羽正 highlight classic arcade game marquee art, specifically detailing the promotional visuals for Taito’s *Metal Black* and Seibu Kaihatsu’s 1990 title *Raiden*. The *Metal Black* description emphasizes its dynamic sci-fi imagery, featuring a monstrous alien, a futuristic spaceship, and the tagline "Final Peace Weapon" against a vibrant purple and orange sky. Conversely, the *Raiden* marquee is noted for its striking red-and-black color scheme, highlighting its claim as a "next-generation shooting game" with simultaneous two-player support. Both summaries focus on specific textual elements, such as Japanese katakana titles and copyright information, to capture the distinct artistic styles and marketing claims of these vintage arcade titles.
